newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-GARCIA OUTDUELS MARTINEZ AS ASTROS CLAIM FIRST PLACE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GARCIA OUTDUELS MARTINEZ AS ASTROS CLAIM FIRST PLACE.

text.p: Ramon Garcia blanked the Expos for eight innings and outduelled Pedro Martinez as the Houston Astros shut down Montreal 2-0 Friday and took sole possession of first place in the National League Central.
Garcia (4-7) scattered six hits and struck out six as he ended a personal three-game losing streak. Billy Wagner pitched a perfect ninth for his 16th save.

"I think he can beat anybody," Houston manager Larry Dierker said of Garcia. "But I wasn't sure we could score off Martinez. He had to go against the best tonight. This is the best start he's had. He had all his pitches working."
The Astros edged over .500 at 49-48 with their fourth win in five games and took a one-game lead over Pittsburgh.
Martinez (11-5), the Expos' ace, went seven innings, allowing seven hits and striking out nine.

Houston picked up its first run in the fourth when Martinez uncharacteristically had trouble finding the plate. He issued three successive walks after Luis Gonzalez doubled. Jeff Bagwell singled in the game's other run in the fifth.

In New York, Butch Huskey's two-run double capped a four-run third inning that was aided by a key error by Deion Sanders and Cincinnati native Joe Crawford earned his first major-league win as the New York Mets defeated the Reds 4-3.

The Mets got all of their runs with two out in the third. With Lance Johnson on first, John Olerud hit a fly down the left-field line. Sanders glided over and was in position for a catch but the ball went under his glove for a two-base error.
After Todd Hundley walked, Edgardo Alfonzo slapped a single to left, scoring Olerud. Huskey then crushed a double off the centre-field wall to score both runners.
Crawford (1-0) got the win with 4 1/3 innings in relief.

"The first major-league win is obviously something special," said Crawford. "I'm from a small town just outside of Cincinnati. I grew up a huge Reds fan. I mean, I love these guys. I know it will be in the papers tomorrow. My mom and dad will get to read it, and you just can't beat it."
In Atlanta, Denny Neagle rebounded from a pair of shaky outings with eight strong innings and Andruw Jones and Fred McGriff homered to power the Atlanta Braves to a 4-1 over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Neagle had given up 10 runs in 10 innings in his last two starts, but he was sharp against the Dodgers, limiting them to one run and five hits with seven strike outs and no walks. His only mistake was a seventh-inning solo homer by Raul Mondesi.
Neagle (13-2) joined teammate Greg Maddux as the only 13-game winners in the National League. Rookie Dennis Reyes (1-1) took the loss for Los Angeles.

At Florida, Mandy Romero, a Miami native appearing in his second major-league game, hit a solo homer and scored twice to lead the San Diego Padres to their sixth win in seven games, a 5-3 victory over the Florida Marlins.

Romero, a 10-year minor leaguer who made his debut Tuesday night, singled for his first big-league hit and scored in the Padres' four-run third inning before leading off the fourth with a homer to right field off starter Alex Fernandez (10-8).
Pete Smith (3-1) went five innings for the win. Tim Worrell worked the ninth, striking out Mark Kotsay and Edgar Renteria with two men on, for his third save.
Renteria homered twice for the Marlins.

In Philadelphia, Mickey Morandini's three-run double capped an eight-run sixth inning in which the Philadelphia Phillies tied a major-league record with three pinch-hit walks on the way to an 8-6 victory over the Pittsburgh Pirates.
Philadelphia used just four hits to plate eight runs in the sixth, aided by six walks.
Phillies starter Mark Leiter (5-10), who had lost his last six decisions, allowed three runs in six innings, struck out nine and walked none to win for the first time since May 20.
Ricky Bottalico pitched two innings for his 16th save.
In St Louis, first baseman Stan Javier's throwing error with the bases loaded in the second allowed two runs to score and the Cardinals held off a late surge to nip the San Francisco Giants 6-5.
After a bases-loaded single by Tom Lampkin gave the Cardinals a 2-1 lead, pitcher Todd Stottlemyre hit a grounder down the line to Javier, normally an outfielder.
Javier stepped on the bag for the first out, but threw wildly to the plate in an attempt at the double play, allowing two runners to score.
Stottlemyre (9-6) got the win. Dennis Eckersley gave up a run in the ninth, but posted his 22nd save by retiring Barry Bonds and Jeff Kent for the final outs with runners on first and second.
Giants starter Shawn Estes (12-4) lost his bid to join Greg Maddux and Denny Neagle of Atlanta as a 13-game winner.
